msg: Duende IdentityServer package or namespace: production use needs a paid Duende licence unless you are Community-eligible (under 1M USD revenue and under 3M USD capital)
oi: OpenIddict.AspNetCore + OpenIddict.EntityFrameworkCore (Apache-2.0, no licence fee); swap the PackageReference and the Duende.IdentityServer.* usings

msg: IdentityServer4 has had no security fixes since 2022-12-13 ({days} days as of {today})
oi: migrate straight to OpenIddict instead of paying for the Duende upgrade

services.AddOpenIddict().AddCore().AddServer().AddAspNetCore() and app.UseAuthentication(); OpenIddict enables no endpoint by default, so call SetTokenEndpointUris("connect/token") and SetAuthorizationEndpointUris("connect/authorize") to keep the URLs your clients call
delete it; OpenIddict has no licence key

seed clients with IOpenIddictApplicationManager.CreateAsync(new OpenIddictApplicationDescriptor { ... }) and scopes with IOpenIddictScopeManager; each AllowedGrantTypes value becomes a Permissions.GrantTypes.* entry and each flow must be switched on (AllowAuthorizationCodeFlow(), AllowClientCredentialsFlow())

options.UseEntityFrameworkCore().UseDbContext<AppDbContext>() plus builder.UseOpenIddict() in the DbContext; the ConfigurationDb and PersistedGrantDb tables do not carry over, so copy clients and scopes with a one-off script
no bridge package: sign users in with ASP.NET Core Identity inside your own /connect/authorize action (EnableAuthorizationEndpointPassthrough()) and return SignIn(principal)

AddDevelopmentEncryptionCertificate() + AddDevelopmentSigningCertificate(); OpenIddict encrypts access tokens by default, so APIs that validate plain JWTs need DisableAccessTokenEncryption() or the OpenIddict validation handler
AddSigningCertificate(cert) plus AddEncryptionCertificate(cert); OpenIddict needs both

msg: Automatic key management left on (no KeyManagement.Enabled = false): Advanced edition, or the 4,000 USD/yr add-on on Standard
oi: OpenIddict does not generate or rotate keys; load signing and encryption certificates yourself and add the next one before the current one expires

msg: Server-side sessions: Standard edition or higher
oi: no built-in equivalent; keep the login session in the ASP.NET Core cookie with a custom ITicketStore (OpenIddict stores tokens and authorizations, not login sessions)
set claims on the ClaimsPrincipal in your authorize/token handler and route each one with SetDestinations()

msg: Duende BFF is licensed separately; without a key BFF v4 runs in trial mode capped at 5 sessions per host
oi: no OpenIddict package; use ASP.NET Core cookie auth with the OpenIddict client and proxy API calls through YARP

msg: Dynamic client registration: Standard edition or higher
oi: OpenIddict ships no registration endpoint; expose your own admin API over IOpenIddictApplicationManager

msg: CIBA backchannel login ({found}): Standard edition or higher
oi: OpenIddict has no CIBA endpoint; move the flow to the device authorization flow or keep it on a separate server

msg: Mutual TLS client authentication: Standard edition or higher
oi: confirm the OpenIddict version you target supports mTLS client authentication before cutover and keep the certificate forwarding middleware
register each upstream login with AddOpenIdConnect() or the OpenIddict client at startup; OpenIddict has no runtime provider store
